title: Perfection over a flat local map with regular closed fibre
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a homomorphism of nonzero commutative local rings, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_R,\mathfrak m_B$, such that the inverse image of $\mathfrak m_B$ is $\mathfrak m_R$. Assume this homomorphism is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose that the closed fibre ring $B/\mathfrak m_RB$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], of Krull dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$. Let $K\in D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Derived tensors use K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Let $a\leq b$ be integers. If $H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)=0$ for every $i\notin[a,b]$, then $K$ is perfect over $B$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] and has Tor amplitude in $[a-d,b]$ over $B$: for every $B$-module $N$ in degree zero, $H^j(K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $j\notin[a-d,b]$. Neither $R$ nor $B$ is required to be Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 09PC, lemma-perfect-over-regular-local-ring, residue-field version of assumption (4) and conclusion.

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above finite-free $B$-complex $P^\bullet$ representing $K$, by pseudo-coherence. Each $P^i\cong B^{n_i}$ is $R$-flat: tensoring an $R$-module injection with it is a finite direct sum of tensoring that injection with the flat $R$-module $B$. The same argument over $B$ makes its terms $B$-flat. The bounded-flat lemma makes $P^\bullet$ K-flat over both rings. Put $C=B/\mathfrak m_RB$ and let $E\in D(C)$ be represented by $P^\bullet\otimes_B C$. Termwise, $P^\bullet\otimes_B C\cong P^\bullet\otimes_R k$, via $p\otimes(b\otimes t)\mapsto bp\otimes t$, using $C\cong B\otimes_R k$. K-flat computation of change of rings over $R$ therefore identifies the underlying $k$-complex of $E$ with $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k$. The hypothesis gives $H^q(E)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. In particular $E$ is cohomologically bounded, although $P^\bullet$ may be unbounded to the left.

source.place: Tag 09PC, lemma-perfect-over-regular-local-ring, proof: finite-free replacement and the paragraph after the displayed tensor equalities; ordinary-module K-flatness Tag 064K, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism, and derived tensor Tag 064M, definition-derived-tor.

proof.text: Put $\ell=B/\mathfrak m_B$. Locality gives $\mathfrak m_RB\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$, so $\ell$ is a $C$-module via the quotient map $C\to\ell$, and is the residue field of $C$. The complex $P^\bullet\otimes_B C$ is bounded above and finite free over $C$, hence K-flat by the bounded-flat lemma. Compute the derived scalar extensions of $K$ along $B\to\ell$ and of $E$ along $C\to\ell$ on these K-flat models. The chain isomorphism $(P^\bullet\otimes_B C)\otimes_C\ell\cong P^\bullet\otimes_B\ell$ sends $(p\otimes c)\otimes t$ to $p\otimes ct$, with inverse $p\otimes t\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes t$; both maps commute with the differential on $P^\bullet$. Consequently $E\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}\ell\cong K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}\ell$ in $D(\ell)$.

source.place: Tag 09PC, lemma-perfect-over-regular-local-ring, proof: the three displayed tensor equalities.

proof.text: The regular-local global-dimension theorem applied to $C$ gives every $C$-module a projective resolution of length at most $d$. In particular, for any $C$-module $M$, choose such a resolution of $M$ to compute $\operatorname{Tor}^C_t(M,\ell)$. Its tensor with $\ell$ has no terms in homological degrees $t>d$, so these Tor modules vanish there. This is the definition of Tor using a projective resolution, not an assumption that $R$ or $B$ is Noetherian. The regular local ring $C$ is Noetherian by its assumed regularity, which is all the global-dimension theorem requires.

source.place: Tag 09PC, lemma-perfect-over-regular-local-ring, proof: finite global dimension of the closed fibre, using algebra.tex Tag 00O7, proposition-regular-finite-gl-dim, and Tag 00LY, section-tor.

proof.text: Apply the bounded tensor-Tor spectral sequence over $C$ to $E$ and $\ell[0]$. Its boundedness hypotheses concern cohomology: step 1 gives $E\in D^b(C)$, and $\ell[0]$ is concentrated in degree zero. Thus its second page is $E_2^{p,q}=\operatorname{Tor}_{-p}^C(H^q(E),\ell)$. Step 3 and the convention of zero Tor in negative homological degrees imply $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless $-d\le p\le0$; step 1 gives zero unless $a\le q\le b$. Hence every position of total degree $n\notin[a-d,b]$ vanishes on the second page. Each later page at that position is a subquotient of the preceding page, so it too vanishes. The cited convergence supplies a finite exhaustive separated filtration of $H^n(E\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}\ell)$ with these zero stable-page modules as graded quotients. Successive equalities of adjacent filtration terms, from the whole module to zero, force that cohomology module to vanish. By step 2, $H^n(K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}\ell)=0$ for $n\notin[a-d,b]$.

source.place: Tag 09PC, lemma-perfect-over-regular-local-ring, final spectral-sequence argument; bounded formulation Tag 0H7Z, lemma-kunneth-spectral-sequence, with finite filtration from Tag 0H7Y, proposition-kunneth-filtered (the source uses the equivalent one-module spectral sequence Tag 061Z).

proof.text: The local ring $B$ has only the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$, so step 4 verifies the residue-field vanishing hypothesis for every maximal ideal of $B$. The object $K$ is pseudo-coherent by assumption, and $a-d\le b$ because $a\le b$ and $d\ge0$. Apply the pseudo-coherent maximal-fibre criterion over $B$, with interval $[a-d,b]$. It gives both that $K$ is perfect over $B$ and that $H^j(K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $B$-module $N$ and every $j\notin[a-d,b]$, as asserted. This criterion imposes no Noetherian hypothesis on $B$.
